key_insight: The paper certifies that a mechanistic edit can provably remove one skill while preserving another across an entire continuous input region, rather than only demonstrating it on sampled tests.
engineering_relevance: This enables safer model editing and unlearning workflows by turning behavioral claims about ablations, weight edits, or activation steering into formal guarantees suitable for verification-oriented deployment.
method: Define the desired skill-removal and skill-preservation behavior as a decidable specification over input regions.
Use sound verification and bound-propagation methods to prove non-interference after editing, including on transformer-style architectures.
Show that black-box testing alone cannot certify removal by constructing an edit that evades exhaustive finite tests but fails on a small survivor pocket.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports certified results from toy ReLU networks up to a standard softmax + LayerNorm transformer, with sound bound propagation scaling to roughly 9x the perturbation dimension an exact solver can handle.
watch_item: The guarantees apply only to small standard-architecture networks and depend on the target skill having a decidable specification, which may not exist for some real-world harms.
paper_title: Certified Mechanistic Edits: Behavioral Guarantees for Skill Removal and Preservation
